reading.body:
Captions offers AI video editing with eye contact correction, dubbing, and likeness manipulation features, positioning these as consent-managed tools rather than uncontrolled synthetic media.

The company operates in a space where video generation capability has outpaced legal frameworks. Eye contact correction and digital likeness creation are computationally straightforward once trained on video data, but their deployment involves consent and identity questions that law has not yet fully resolved. New York's 311 law exposure entries suggest regulatory attention, though the data does not specify whether these are proposed bills, existing statutes, or cases.

For AI infrastructure, this matters because video tools sit at the intersection of compute demand and legal constraint. Rendering edited video and training models for likeness manipulation require significant processing. If regulation tightens around synthetic media, it may shift not whether these tools exist, but where they run and who can access their models. The data does not clarify Captions' training or inference infrastructure, so it cannot speak to compute or power requirements directly.

The consent framing in the product notes is notable. It suggests the company has chosen a regulatory posture rather than a technical one, making human approval a feature rather than a barrier. This does not tell us whether that approach will survive legal scrutiny in New York or elsewhere.

profile_text.body:
Captions is an AI video generator and editor founded in 2021 and based in New York City. According to its website, the company describes itself as offering "AI That Edits Like a Professional Editor," providing tools that make it easy to go from idea to ready-to-share content regardless of user skillset. The platform handles time-consuming editing tasks automatically, cutting scenes, overlaying B-roll, auto-generating captions, and generating translated subtitles. Users can upload existing footage for AI editing or generate entirely new footage without recording, with the AI understanding the story and tailoring edits to specific footage.

Captions AI's product capabilities include creating AI twins or selecting from digital avatars for video generation, with users able to iterate quickly using the same avatar across different topics and videos. The platform serves a range of content types, including short-form social videos, ads, tutorials, product demos, real estate listing videos, and talking head videos. Its feature set encompasses prompt-to-video and script-to-video generation, text-based video editing, B-roll integration, and transition editing.

The company operates in a jurisdiction with significant AI regulation exposure, holding regulatory presence in New York State.
